risk_of_bias.note: Overall high is carried by the deviations domain and is not less severe than the worst domain, as METHODS 5.3 requires. The design label (human-laboratory) and RoB 2 match the project's mapping, and the order of the two route conditions was balanced, so RoB 2 is defensible here; the absence of a placebo condition is handled inside the domains rather than by changing the instrument.

risk_of_bias_domains.domain: Randomization process (order of the two route conditions)
risk_of_bias_domains.note: Balanced crossover is stated on p. 476 with no sequence generation, concealment or period term; some-concerns fits.
The authors themselves say the concurrent intravenous dose and unequal delivered doses confound the between-route pharmacodynamic comparison (pp. 480, 485); high fits.

All 8 completed. Under RoB 2 the exclusion of one tmax from the only test of that difference belongs in domain 5 rather than domain 3, but the judgment is unchanged and domain 5 already carries concerns.
Validated assay and monitored vital signs against unblinded self-reports; some-concerns fits.
No protocol, and the 67% figure appears in no table; verified that only Table II prints 37.4 and 79.4.

interpretation_gap.note: The numbers in the abstract do match averages of the two tabulated conditions rather than any printed row, and the authors state the pharmacodynamic limits themselves; a minor gap is right. The one unsupported claim (complications) is already named in the card.

missed: Reporting error not recorded: Table VI (p. 482) prints the intravenous clearance for the intranasal session as 284 (SD 59.0) mL/h/kg, while Table I (p. 481) gives 272 (SD 73.3) for the same 10 mg infusion; Table VI's asterisked rows apply that intravenous clearance to the nasal and smoked rows, so the printed percent-of-dose-excreted values depend on which of the two clearances is used.

Exposure field: the card places the limits of quantification (10 ng/mL methamphetamine, 1 ng/mL amphetamine) in plasma, but both sentences stand at the end of the urine assay paragraph (p. 478), and the plasma precision data run down to 1 ng/mL for methamphetamine, so a plasma limit of 10 ng/mL is not established by the paper.

Selection effect not named: every participant smoked tobacco and continued to do so (p. 476); tobacco use bears both on urine pH, which the card itself flags as uncontrolled, and on familiarity with inhalation technique in the smoked condition.
The 2008 entry in the replication timeline cannot be checked against this source (its reference list ends in 2003); it needs checking elsewhere before the card leaves first-pass.
